applies_why: Yes -- the judge text adjudicates exactly the collision K-C governs: [DR3] link 6 presses the defender's Isaiah 7:14 link with the challenger's own chain read together, so the collision must be weighed chain against chain by footing.
quote: D3 vs C6 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] answered the Isaiah 8:3-4 bound with 8:8 and 9:6-7, while [DR3] presses the sign's own bounds; the sign itself does not state the mechanism.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires... for either side': on one reading the judge's final clause is a mere shared observation (the challenger's own link 6 says the sign announces without explaining, and the defender rests on Matthew's fulfilment rather than the sign's own words), so UNDERDETERMINED flows from two chains that each answered the other; on the other reading the clause is the operative ground, the judge resolving the collision by what 'the sign itself' -- a single witness -- fails to state in its own words instead of weighing the two chains' footing. I weighed the shared-observation reading against the operative-ground reading and adopted the latter, because the clause is the verdict's last, load-bearing reason and no comparison of footing appears anywhere in the text.
why: The judge grounded the verdict in the sign's own failure to state the mechanism in its own words -- the retired stating-verse test -- instead of weighing the defender's chain (8:8, 9:6-7, parthenos, Matthew 1:22) against the challenger's chain (7:16, 8:3-4, the almah/bethulah counts) by footing, so the text breaches K-C.
